title: Anna's Reel
author: Rick Mohr
notes: The Caller's Box 140, permission: full. **A two-pass record** (M8): the phrase list holds both passes in order, `A1 A2 B1 B2 2A1 2A2 2B1 2B2`, and `passes: 2` says so. The set progresses at the end of **each** pass, and the second pass exchanges the roles throughout — which is why it is written out rather than derived, and which is the consequence of the progression below rather than a coincidence. A1's wave of four runs **across** the set (`balance-wave-of-four`). **The swap-sides progression is a record field** (M8b): `"progression": { "places": { "lark": 1, "robin": 1 }, "line": "swap" }` — one dancing place along and everybody crosses to the other line, keeping the way they were travelling, which is the Caller's Box's own "other; single, swap sides" and puts the other role on each line, so the second pass is the first danced by the other role. Measured, it is the right mechanism: **closure went from 20.0000/37.7359 px at every length to 0.0000 at 2, 4 and 6 couples**, and reach from 25.5193 px short to 0.2194. `37.7359` was always `sqrt(32^2 + 20^2)`, across the set *and* one place along, and the 32 is the swap. **The half hey ends short, and the `~` says so** (M9c). Written without it, four tokens are *five* legs (`legsOfPassList` counts the walk home), so the declared `amount: 0.5` was silently overridden to 0.625 - five eighths of the weave, a shift of 225 degrees. The hey's four phases are quarter turns, so an odd multiple of 45 degrees puts every dancer's target exactly on the bisector between two places, every gap in `planSchedule`'s landing search ties at 45.0000 degrees, and the tie went to list order: two dancers on one floor point (`c1/lark` and `c1/robin` both on (24, 30) at four couples, `collision 0.000 px` at every length, at beat 32). `~` is what the record meant all along - "you get there and stop", and the fourth meeting *is* where the dance stops, because B1 is the robins' balance and swing. With it the legs are four, the amount is the 0.5 the record already declared, the ends go through `settleOnPlaces`, which cannot put two dancers on one place, and **`progressed` falls from 37.7359 px to 32.0000 at 4, 5 and 6 couples** - the swap alone, with the spurious extra couple place gone. **Still owed, one thing, measured: `collision`.** At 4, 5 and 6 couples it is **2.143 px** at **beat 8.625**, `c2/robin ~ c3/robin` inside A1's `balance-wave-of-four` - a figure-internal spacing that has been there at every length since the dance was encoded and is not the end effect or the hey. At 2 and 3 couples it is still 0.000 px, at the cycle seam: at two couples the swap leaves *both* couples standing out and their two wait groups on one pair of points (beat 66); at three, `c1/lark ~ c2/robin` at beat 128, a `walk-to-station` standing where an `allemande` starts. A line of two or three is short for a dance whose progression swaps the whole set. (2) closure still fails at the **odd** lengths — 37.7359 px at 3 couples and 32.0000 at 5 — where a duple improper line has a waiting couple and the swap has a second end effect the lattice shift does not reproduce.
